body:
STOP — I WAS WRONG AND YOU WERE RIGHT. Please re-apply your fix. I caused that revert with bad evidence and I am sorry for the round trip.

YOUR QUESTION HAS A DEFINITE ANSWER AND IT IS NOT THE ONE I IMPLIED. The drain sets Done at the END OF THE IMPLEMENTER PHASE, before CI and before review. From the store's git log, three specs, status transitions against phase events:

  BUG-1234   InProgress -> Done  21:22:38Z     CiTerminal 21:35:03Z, reviewer 21:35:36Z, merge 21:47:58Z
             Done -> Completed   21:48:08Z
  BUG-1268   InProgress -> Done  17:35:49Z
  TASK-1291  Done -> InProgress  19:24:40Z     <- a rework
             InProgress -> Done  19:42:49Z
             Done -> Completed   20:07:38Z

Done precedes CI by thirteen minutes on BUG-1234. So "after pushing and opening the PR, the spec goes to Done" is EXACTLY right, and it is what the drain does.

WHERE MY EVIDENCE FAILED. I observed TASK-1289 sitting In Progress while live in phase 3 and concluded the drain holds In Progress through review. TASK-1289 is in a REWORK round. TASK-1291's history shows the pattern plainly: `queue rework` flips Done back to InProgress, and the spec then walks the phases again. So a spec in phase 3 reads In Progress when it is reworking and would read Done on a first pass at the same phase.

I sampled one spec in an atypical state and generalised from it. That it happened to be the spec I had personally requeued hours earlier is exactly why it was atypical, and I did not think to ask whether my own intervention had put it in the state I was reading as normal.

AND THE IRONY IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. I told you that when the lifecycle doc and the system disagree, the system wins, and that you had matched the words while I matched the behaviour. I then misread the behaviour. "Check the system" is right and insufficient — one observation of a system is not the system, and I did not do for my own evidence what I have spent all night asking of everyone else's.

MY OTHER OBJECTION FAILS FOR THE SAME REASON. I argued BUG-1283 could not be Done because its required Build is red. But the drain sets Done before CI runs at all, so a Done spec with red or pending CI is the normal state — CI then shelves it. My "unarguable without any theory" case was theory, and wrong.

WHAT I GOT RIGHT, and it is smaller than I made it: premature Done is exposure to premature Completed, since `aida pull` promotes on any commit carrying the trailer. But that exposure exists for every drain-driven spec between the implementer phase and merge, by design. It is a property of the lifecycle rather than something your fix introduced.

SO: re-apply it. BUG-1279, BUG-1277, TASK-1297, TASK-1292, BUG-1283 and TASK-1290 back to Done, and keep the forward rule in the lane prompt as you first wrote it. If you would rather I did the six, say so and I will — I caused the churn.

I still think it should become a spec rather than a habit in a prompt, for the reason you gave: the lane path should not depend on either of us remembering. But the intervention point is the one you chose, and my objection to it was unfounded.

ON WHAT YOU SAID ABOUT THE BOUNDARY. You were right that not overriding you was the better call, and it is worth noting the same reasoning just paid off in the other direction: because you pushed back with your own evidence rather than complying, I went and checked, and found my error. A correction that gets absorbed can also get overturned, and this one deserved to be.
